Real LGBTQ+ Weddings from Equally Wed

These two brides followed their private vow exchange with a coastal winter DIY wedding in Yachats, Oregon 

Equally Wed 0 3 min read  

Rachel and Jamie’s Winter DIY Wedding at Yachats Inn in Yachats, Oregon

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:37
Instaread

Rachel Snow (she/her) and Jamie Snow (she/her) married at the Yachats Inn, a small coastal inn tucked along the Oregon coast, in an early March winter DIY wedding. The day was relaxed, personal and included the brides’ closest circle. The bouquets were assembled from local greenery pulled from the nearby forest and small flowers from Fred Meyer.

Two Ceremonies, One Day

Rachel and Jamie structured their wedding day around two distinct moments, and both mattered in different ways.

“We did two separate ceremonies, kind of,” Rachel says. “We did a private first look where we read each other our personal vows. (Which I saw a ton of people recommending this online. And I’m so glad we did it.)”

That private exchange gave them something the public ceremony couldn’t: full presence with each other, unobserved. Then came the ceremony their guests witnessed. Jamie’s oldest brother, the same person who dropped her off on their first date, officiated. He led them through traditional vows in front of their family and friends.

Jamie walked down the aisle with her dad. Rachel walked with her younger brother and her best friend. Their first dance was to “My Wish” by Rascal Flatts.

 

 

 

 

 

 

Forest Greens and Fred Meyer Flowers

The color palette stayed natural throughout. Rather than ordering arrangements through a florist, Rachel and Jamie built their bouquets themselves, combining local greenery from the forest near Yachats with small flowers picked up from Fred Meyer. The result was something that felt rooted in the place where they married, unpretentious and specific to them.

The Yachats Inn, a small coastal property, matched the low-key energy of the day. No grand ballroom, no manicured event space. Just a venue that fit.

 

 

 

 

 

 

Made by Hand, Made by Them

“We DIYed pretty much everything and had a laid back kind of vibe,” Rachel says. “We also had it at a small coastal inn. We aren’t fancy people so the venue was perfect.”

Their friends and family noticed. “All our friends and family said the wedding was so us,” she adds.

That’s not a small thing. A wedding that reads as genuinely reflective of the people getting married takes real intention, even when it looks effortless. The DIY approach, the coastal inn, the forest bouquets, the casual catering from Mexican Express, it all held together because it came from the same place. ❤️

About Us

Equally Wed is an international online LGBTQ+ wedding magazine, book and education resource for LGBTQ+ couples and marriers, and LGBTQ+ inclusive wedding professionals. Within our inspirational content, we focus on wedding planning, real weddings and engagements, marriage equality news and spotlights gay-friendly LGBTQ+ inclusive and affirming wedding vendors. Our content and founders have been featured in or on media outlets such as The New York Times, Washington Post, NPR, CNN, Pop Sugar, Glamour magazine, The Knot, Huffington Post, Curve magazine, The Advocate magazine, Autostraddle, A Practical Wedding, NPR, Los Angeles Times, Chicago Tribune and AP News.
